en.title: Integers with No Repeated Digits in a Range
en.description:
For each closed interval [n,m], count the positive integers whose decimal representation has all distinct digits. 0 is a digit too, and appearing twice counts as a repeat; no leading zeros are added.

The input and output format was prepared by this site.
en.input: This site's simplified input protocol: the first line contains q, followed by q lines each with two integers n m (the fixed column count 2 of the original function wrapper is omitted). 1≤q≤100000, 1≤n≤m≤1000000.
en.output: Output one count per line, in query order.
en.explanation: From 1 to 20 only 11 is invalid, giving 19; from 98 to 102 only 98 and 102 are valid; the single points 10 and 123 are both valid, while 100 is invalid because 0 repeats.
hints: Use a bitmask to determine whether the digits of each number from 1 up to the largest right endpoint repeat, building prefix counts at the same time; the answer for an interval is pre[m]−pre[n−1].
